45.58: \C\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\AHe that treads foolishly into the sacred\Nkeep shall reap the pain of a thousand\Ncrushed souls!
45.59: \CHear my words, Releaser. I have\Ncome to be known as Jeal. I am also\None of the seven guardians\W2\AI was a metalsmith who sought to\Nunderstand the mysteries of life.\N\ATo stop the evil present in the mortal\Nrealm, I sacrificed my human form\Nand vanished into time. \AI have given thought to trusting the\Nlight of your soul to save this weary\Nland.\AHowever,\W2\T\W2\Tyou must bear\Nin mind that to defeat Melzas is to\Nrisk the end of reality itself!\A\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2If you can bear\Nthat risk, proceed.\N
45.69: \BThe lettering on the tombstone\Nhas worn over time.
45.70: \BLet the light of guidance show the\Nsign of contact\W2
45.71: \BPlease give me the life which is\Nborn of fire\W2
45.72: \BBless the destroyer of evil who\Nhides within the flowing waters\W2
45.73: \BYou petition the guardians to\Nopen the doors.\ARight Door:\AAsk the one up and on the other side.\N\ACentre Door:\AAsk the one to the left and at the\Ntop class and the one on the right\Nsecond from the bottom .\ALeft Door:\AAsk the one closest.
45.81: \BThe wall is flawed by a deep fissure.
45.83: \CI see\T\W2\T\W2it has all become\Ncrystal clear\W2You are the\NReleaser, Alundra.
45.84: \COne who's inner strength and resolve\Nis as potent as yours is a rare find,\Nindeed.\AIf you have resolved to fight to the\Ndeath, you may be able to challenge\NMelzas himself.
45.90: \EThis pump is the heart of our great\Nwaterway. We will never allow one\Nto destroy it! Die, trespasser!
45.91: \BThere is a distant sound of gurgling\Nwater.
45.92: \BThe water is too deep. Further access\Nis impossible\W2
45.95: \DI am at once amazed and proud that\Nyou have progressed this far,\NReleaser.\AI am Stenia, Queen of the waters.\NYour actions have been shown to\Nmy heart by the rivers and oceans.\AOver the course of human history,\Nthere have been many gods.\N\ANot long ago, there was a race of\Ngiant gods called the Gazeck.\N\AYou have met one of them\W2Nirude.\NThe Gazeck were carved from stone\Nby the hands of ancient humans.\AThe seven Gazeck were revered and\Nfeared by the ancients\W2\N\ASoon, their prayers gave life to the\NGazecks. They literally became\Nwhat humans believed them to be.\ABut the Gazeck did not want to share\Nthe power of human prayer.\N\AThey fought each other for it\W2they\Nkilled each other for the prize of\Nhuman adulation.\AAll but one of them perished. \TOnly\NNirude declined to fight his fellow\Ngods.\AHe watched with a heavy heart as his\Nbrothers slaughtered one another.\N\ABut when the killing subsided, Nirude\Nfound that he was a god no more.\N\AThe ancient humans had long since\Nlost faith in the warring Gazeck.\N\AAnd, a god cannot exist without the\Nfaith of others\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\N\ASoon, another god was born from the\Nprayers of the people.\T That one was\T\N\W2Melzas.\ABut he was not the god of eternal\Npeace for which the humans had\Nprayed.\AHe was even more flawed than the\NGazecks had become, using fear to\Ngain the faith of humans.\ABut Melzas feared the wisdom of\Nhumans. He knew that they could\Nstrip him of power.\ATherefore, he began slaying\Nwhomever seemed to threaten his\Nexistence.\ASomehow, you have managed to\Nescape his machinations to this\Npoint\W2\A\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2
45.96: \DMelzas has been watching us,\NAlundra. He has used my own water\Nagainst me\W2Take this, Alundra!
45.97: \DMelzas will soon destroy this\Nplace.\A\999\Y\ALeave here, Alundra! You must\Nhurry! The destruction comes!\N
45.98: \BA low rumble of falling rocks can\Nbe heard.
45.100: \BHe that does not fear the flame\Nshall gain mastery over it for\Nall eternity.
45.101: \CWhat have we here?\AYet another greedy human seeking\Nto claim the power of flame for\Nhimself?\AAll right, foolish one. Let's play a\Ngame of skill with my ball of\Neternal damnation!\APrepare to come to terms with your\Nlimitations, human!\N
45.103: \CYou're different from those that\Nhave come before\W2but you have\Nnot proven yourself worthy, yet.\AFollow the course of wisdom\Nemblazoned within your very soul\Nto meet your destiny.
45.104: \CIn the shadow of flame your\Npath must lie, until the time the\Nmotion dies\W2
45.105: \CIf you fail to finish upon the sign\Nof the flame, the power shall not\Nremain yours to command.
45.107: \CYou have indeed proven yourself\Na master of the flame! Take this\Nas proof of your mastery!
45.108: \CMay the power of flame never\Nleave your command!

46.54: \BWith the blessing of the Four\NGoddesses, show my kingdom\Nyour courage.
46.55: \BYou are the one who has been\Nblessed\W2Let me show you the\Nway!
46.56: \BWithout a key to unlock it, there's\Nno chance of it moving.
46.58: \C\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\AHe that treads foolishly into the sacred\Nkeep shall reap the pain of a thousand\Ncrushed souls!
46.59: \CHear my words, Releaser. I have\Ncome to be known as Jeal. I am also\None of the seven guardians\W2\AI was a metalsmith who sought to\Nunderstand the mysteries of life.\N\ATo stop the evil present in the mortal\Nrealm, I sacrificed my human form\Nand vanished into time. \AI have given thought to trusting the\Nlight of your soul to save this weary\Nland.\AHowever,\W2\T\W2\Tyou must bear\Nin mind that to defeat Melzas is to\Nrisk the end of reality itself!\A\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2If you can bear\Nthat risk, proceed.\N
46.69: \BThe lettering on the tombstone\Nhas worn over time.
46.70: \BLet the light of guidance show the\Nsign of contact\W2
46.71: \BPlease give me the life which is\Nborn of fire\W2
46.72: \BBless the destroyer of evil who\Nhides within the flowing waters\W2
46.73: \BYou petition the guardians to\Nopen the doors.\ARight Door:\AAsk the one up and on the other side.\N\ACentre Door:\AAsk the one to the left and at the\Ntop class and the one on the right\Nsecond from the bottom .\ALeft Door:\AAsk the one closest.
46.81: \BThe wall is flawed by a deep fissure.
46.83: \CI see\T\W2\T\W2it has all become\Ncrystal clear\W2You are the\NReleaser, Alundra.
46.84: \COne who's inner strength and resolve\Nis as potent as yours is a rare find,\Nindeed.\AIf you have resolved to fight to the\Ndeath, you may be able to challenge\NMelzas himself.
46.90: \EThis pump is the heart of our great\Nwaterway. We will never allow one\Nto destroy it! Die, trespasser!
46.91: \BThere is a distant sound of gurgling\Nwater.
46.92: \BThe water is too deep. Further access\Nis impossible\W2
46.95: \DI am at once amazed and proud that\Nyou have progressed this far,\NReleaser.\AI am Stenia, Queen of the waters.\NYour actions have been shown to\Nmy heart by the rivers and oceans.\AOver the course of human history,\Nthere have been many gods.\N\ANot long ago, there was a race of\Ngiant gods called the Gazeck.\N\AYou have met one of them\W2Nirude.\NThe Gazeck were carved from stone\Nby the hands of ancient humans.\AThe seven Gazeck were revered and\Nfeared by the ancients\W2\N\ASoon, their prayers gave life to the\NGazecks. They literally became\Nwhat humans believed them to be.\ABut the Gazeck did not want to share\Nthe power of human prayer.\N\AThey fought each other for it\W2they\Nkilled each other for the prize of\Nhuman adulation.\AAll but one of them perished. \TOnly\NNirude declined to fight his fellow\Ngods.\AHe watched with a heavy heart as his\Nbrothers slaughtered one another.\N\ABut when the killing subsided, Nirude\Nfound that he was a god no more.\N\AThe ancient humans had long since\Nlost faith in the warring Gazeck.\N\AAnd, a god cannot exist without the\Nfaith of others\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\N\ASoon, another god was born from the\Nprayers of the people.\T That one was\T\N\W2Melzas.\ABut he was not the god of eternal\Npeace for which the humans had\Nprayed.\AHe was even more flawed than the\NGazecks had become, using fear to\Ngain the faith of humans.\ABut Melzas feared the wisdom of\Nhumans. He knew that they could\Nstrip him of power.\ATherefore, he began slaying\Nwhomever seemed to threaten his\Nexistence.\ASomehow, you have managed to\Nescape his machinations to this\Npoint\W2\A\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2
46.96: \DMelzas has been watching us,\NAlundra. He has used my own water\Nagainst me\W2Take this, Alundra!
46.97: \DMelzas will soon destroy this\Nplace.\A\999\Y\ALeave here, Alundra! You must\Nhurry! The destruction comes!\N
46.98: \BA low rumble of falling rocks can\Nbe heard.
46.100: \BHe that does not fear the flame\Nshall gain mastery over it for\Nall eternity.

47.0: \CSara\T\W2\T\W2\TSara! Don't be shy,\Nyou tasty morsel of babitude! Let me\Ncheck you out!
47.1: \DHere I am, you Greek god. Come to\Nme, Bonaire. Hurry\T\W2\T\N\W2\Thurry!
47.3: \C\W2\T\W2\TDude! Where am I\Ngoing? I'm in a most heinous state\Nof confusion\W2
47.4: \CAre you totally trying to guide me\Nsomewhere?
47.5: \DIndeed I am, hunky buns. I am\Ntaking you to the gates of rapturous\Nparadise.
47.6: \DGo through that door. That's it\T\W2\N\W2\TAlmost there, my sweet.
47.7: \D\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2!Make haste,\Ndarling Bonaire! Someone lies in\Nwait to snatch me from you!\N\999\Y
47.8: \CThat is totally not going to happen!\NNothing can keep us apart, Sara!\AI would pass up the most righteous\Nswell for you! Bhuh\W2at least I think\NI would\W2\999\Y
47.9: \D\W2\T\W2\TAlmost there.\AJust a few more short steps until we\Ncan intertwine our taut, supple\Nflesh forever, darling Bonaire.\999\Y
47.10: \DI am the crusher of souls! I am\Nimmortal! And worse\W2\T\W2\T\W2\NI am really cheesed off!
47.11: \DNo one messes with Sara and lives to\Nspeak of it! Let some of my closest\Nghouls impress this upon you!
47.12: \DCome hither, Waverunner. You'll\Nmake a fine snack!\AWhat\T\W2\T\W2\TWho are you?\NOr rather\W2WHAT are you?\N
47.13: \DI'm glad you're here\W2I don't think\NWaveboy has the\W2 meat to satisfy\Nmy appetite.\APerhaps I should turn to someone\Nmore, mmm\W2substantial...\W2\N\A
47.14: \DWhat's that? You're here to rescue\NSurfer Boy?\AToo late, punk! Bonaire is all mine!\NPerhaps we can strike another\Nbargain instead\W2\ASubmit to me and I'll spare your\Nlife, making you my love slave\W2\N\AUnfortunately, when I tire of you,\NI shall be forced to devour you\Nanyway\W2
47.15: \C\W2\T\W2\TDude!\NWhat are you doing here?\NWhat am I doing here?\A\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2Where is Sara?\N\N
47.16: \DBonaire, my sweet love muffin!\AI am \W2suffering\W2in such\N\W2such horrible pain\W2\NHelp me, Bonaire!
47.17: \DWhy do you persist in your selfish\Nways? I am offering you my heart,\Nyou jerk!\AI mean, um, \W2you stud!\N\N\AHow can you be so heartless? Look\Nwhat you're doing to me\W2I mean,\N\W2to us?!
47.18: \DYou have betrayed our pure love,\NWaveboy.\AI am, to use one of your choice words\Nof surfdom, bummed.\N\AHowever, I shall not wallow in my\Nbumitude alone\W2oh, no!\N\AI shall steal the soul of one who loves\Nyou perfectly and completely\W2\N\ABut whom you have yet to show any\Naffection\W2\N\ABy the time you realise your true\Nfeelings, she will already be gone!\N
47.101: \CWhere did you go?\NWhere are you going?\NThrow me a bone here!

48.0: \DThis is impossible! How are we going\Nto get across? This chasm is far too\Nwide to jump!
48.1: \DI told you I'd give you a headstart!
48.2: \DWell, what are you waiting for?\Nlead the way! The teleport pad\Nout of here is over there!
48.3: \DAll right, Alundra. Any ideas how\Nwe're going to open the door?
48.4: \DI still can't believe I let you use me for\Na Stairmaster. But, I must admit\W2\Nyou were great!
48.5: \DI've been trying to figure this one\Nout while you were catching up.\AIt seems like each switch that\Nappears creates a corresponding\Nfloor tile when one steps on it.\AWait\W2I have an idea\W2\A
48.6: \DI'll step on the switches, and you leap\Nacross the floor tiles, got it?
48.7: \DLet's try that again, but this time how\Nabout a little concentration, hmmm?
48.8: \DAll right, Alundra. The path to the\Ndoor's open. This is the moment\Nof truth. Let's get to it.
48.9: \DLacking all due respect\W2 that blew,\Nhero boy.\N\AI already explained to you how the\Nswitches trigger the steps.\N\AWatch what I do before you before\Nyou go off leaping into space!\N\A
48.10: \DThere you are, Alundra!\AThis rock seems to be placed rather\Ninconveniently. Any bright ideas\Nhow to overcome this little obstacle?
48.11: \DWell, well\W2you're full of surprises,\Naren't you Alundra?\N
48.12: \DWhat's the matter, Alundra? Having\Na little trouble advancing?\ATense those scrawny neck muscles!\NI'll be needing to use your head,\Nloverboy!
48.13: \DAnd the way is revealed to the\Nfaithful! Let's go!
48.14: \DYou're late, Alundra. What's the\Nmatter? Gonna let a girl best you?\N\AHere's a chance to redeem yourself,\Nagain. Help me release the trap in\Nthis room.\AWe have to push the left and right\Nswitches simultaneously. Let's get\Nto it\W2\AWatch me closely, and press your\Nbuttons when I press mine.\N
48.15: \DHello? Alundra? Are you awake? Or\Nhave you succumbed to some kind of\Nweird spastic dream, too?\APay attention and push your switch\Nat the same time that I push mine!\N
48.100: \DAlundra\T\W2\T\W2\TPlease wait for\Nme. I can help you!\N
48.101: \DAlundra, I'm loathe to admit it,\Nbut I'm stumped. Please come and\Nhelp me figure this out\W2
48.102: \DAhh! Now the true test begins\W2\AOur task is to destroy all four of the\Nnightmares that have seized control\Nof her subconscious.\W2\AIf even one remains, I'm afraid Elene\Nis doomed to perish horribly\W2\N
48.103: \DWhich nightmare do you choose\Nto start with?\N\AThe coloured crystal you destroy\Nin the centre appears to determine\Nthe order you attack the dream\W2
48.104: \DThe choice is yours alone to make.\NRegardless of your choice of the\Norder, I will follow.
48.105: \DI can barely get this switch to\Nbudge! There must be a way to gain\Nmore leverage\W2
48.106: \DHmm\W2perhaps if we had a bit\Nmore weight? Where's Roger Ebert\Nwhen you need him?!
48.107: \DAlundra, I swear! I really didn't\Ntake you for the type that treated\Nwomen like doormats\W2
48.108: \DIf only we had a few more pounds!\NCurse my hide for not packing the\Npower bars\W2
48.109: \BWhen land's rage bellows forth,\Nonly the fruit of ages shall silence\Nthe fury\W2

77.72: \BBless the destroyer of evil who\Nhides within the flowing waters\W2

77.81: \BThe wall is flawed by a deep fissure.
77.83: \CI see\T\W2\T\W2it has all become\Ncrystal clear\W2You are the\NReleaser, Alundra.
77.84: \COne who's inner strength and resolve\Nis as potent as yours is a rare find,\Nindeed.\AIf you have resolved to fight to the\Ndeath, you may be able to challenge\NMelzas himself.
77.90: \EThis pump is the heart of our great\Nwaterway. We will never allow one\Nto destroy it! Die, trespasser!
77.91: \BThere is a distant sound of gurgling\Nwater.
77.92: \BThe water is too deep. Further access\Nis impossible\W2
77.95: \DI am at once amazed and proud that\Nyou have progressed this far,\NReleaser.\AI am Stenia, Queen of the waters.\NYour actions have been shown to\Nmy heart by the rivers and oceans.\AOver the course of human history,\Nthere have been many gods.\N\ANot long ago, there was a race of\Ngiant gods called the Gazeck.\N\AYou have met one of them\W2Nirude.\NThe Gazeck were carved from stone\Nby the hands of ancient humans.\AThe seven Gazeck were revered and\Nfeared by the ancients\W2\N\ASoon, their prayers gave life to the\NGazecks. They literally became\Nwhat humans believed them to be.\ABut the Gazeck did not want to share\Nthe power of human prayer.\N\AThey fought each other for it\W2they\Nkilled each other for the prize of\Nhuman adulation.\AAll but one of them perished. \TOnly\NNirude declined to fight his fellow\Ngods.\AHe watched with a heavy heart as his\Nbrothers slaughtered one another.\N\ABut when the killing subsided, Nirude\Nfound that he was a god no more.\N\AThe ancient humans had long since\Nlost faith in the warring Gazeck.\N\AAnd, a god cannot exist without the\Nfaith of others\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\N\ASoon, another god was born from the\Nprayers of the people.\T That one was\T\N\W2Melzas.\ABut he was not the god of eternal\Npeace for which the humans had\Nprayed.\AHe was even more flawed than the\NGazecks had become, using fear to\Ngain the faith of humans.\ABut Melzas feared the wisdom of\Nhumans. He knew that they could\Nstrip him of power.\ATherefore, he began slaying\Nwhomever seemed to threaten his\Nexistence.\ASomehow, you have managed to\Nescape his machinations to this\Npoint\W2\A\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2
77.96: \DMelzas has been watching us,\NAlundra. He has used my own water\Nagainst me\W2Take this, Alundra!
77.97: \DMelzas will soon destroy this\Nplace.\A\999\Y\ALeave here, Alundra! You must\Nhurry! The destruction comes!\N
77.98: \BA low rumble of falling rocks can\Nbe heard.
77.100: \BHe that does not fear the flame\Nshall gain mastery over it for\Nall eternity.
77.101: \CWhat have we here?\AYet another greedy human seeking\Nto claim the power of flame for\Nhimself?\AAll right, foolish one. Let's play a\Ngame of skill with my ball of\Neternal damnation!\APrepare to come to terms with your\Nlimitations, human!\N
77.103: \CYou're different from those that\Nhave come before\W2but you have\Nnot proven yourself worthy, yet.\AFollow the course of wisdom\Nemblazoned within your very soul\Nto meet your destiny.
77.104: \CIn the shadow of flame your\Npath must lie, until the time the\Nmotion dies\W2
77.105: \CIf you fail to finish upon the sign\Nof the flame, the power shall not\Nremain yours to command.
77.107: \CYou have indeed proven yourself\Na master of the flame! Take this\Nas proof of your mastery!
77.108: \CMay the power of flame never\Nleave your command!

134.0: \CHey, kid. I'm amazed you survived\Nthe shipwreck. I had a feeling you'd\Nland on your feet\W2\AWhat am I doing here? I invested the\Ntreasure from my years of adventure\Ninto this shop.\AOne very near-fatal shipwreck is all\NI needed to make me think long and\Nhard about a career change\W2
134.1: \CWell, kid, aren't you going to buy\Nsomething?
134.2: \CLife Vessel? That's 10000 Gilder.\NWould you like it?\0100\Y
134.3: \COlga's Ring, eh? That's pretty nice,\Nbut it's gonna cost you dearly. I'll say\N10000 Gilder. Still want it?\0100\Y
134.4: \CThat Silver Armlet is quite a rare\Ntreasure! I'll part with it for 10000\NGilder. Deal?\0100\Y
134.5: \CRecovery Ring? 10000 Gilder.\NShall I wrap it up?\0100\Y
134.6: \CAh! I see you have your heart set on the\NSpirit Wand. That'll run you 10000\NGilder. Can you afford it?\0100\Y
134.7: \CKid, either you're trying to be quite\Nfunny, or just being trying. Either\Nway, I'm less than amused.
134.8: \CDid you say Gilded Falcon? Yes, I\Nknow of those treasures, who\Ndoesn't?\ALong ago, I took to the seas just to find\Nthe falcons legend's spoke of as being\Nscattered all over the world...\ATo find them all would have made\Nme a legend myself, and rich beyond\Nhuman comprehension!
134.9: \CKid, if you happen to find any of the\NGilded Falcons and bring them to\Nme, I'll trade you items for them.\AIt's a pretty sweet deal. You bring me\Nwhat I want, I'll trade you for the\Nitems you need and desire. Deal?\0100\Y
134.10: \CWhen you change your mind\W2and\NI know you will\W2come back again.
134.12: \CAh, Alundra! I knew from the\Nmoment I laid eyes on your greenish\Nface at sea you were something special!\AI am a very happy man. Thank you,\NAlundra!\N
134.13: \CLet me count how many falcons you're\Ntrading in\W2hmm\W2You've brought\Nme \X0 today.
134.14: \CWell, let's see. That means you've\Nbrought me \X1 Gilded Falcons so\Nfar.
134.15: \CYou have presented me with \X1\NGilded Falcons. Please accept this\Ngift as my thanks to you, Alundra.
134.16: \CI think you'll find this \X2\Nquite useful. Use it in good health,\NAlundra!
134.18: \CNo Gilded Falcons to brighten my\Ncountenance today, Alundra? I can't\Nsay I'm not disappointed\W2
134.19: \CBring me \X3 Falcon Statuettes\Nand I'll reward you with this:\N\X4.\0100\Y
134.20: \CYou need \X5 more Gilded Falcons\Nto claim your reward.
134.21: \CBehold the next gift I hold out as a\Nreward for a cache of Gilded Falcons,\NAlundra!
134.22: \CI don't think I'll be collecting any more\Nstatuettes, kid.\AMy fortune-teller told me that I may\Nhave angered the gods with my\Ngreed.\AI'd rather not remain in that\Nuncomfortable state.
134.23: \CYou're making me nervous, kid. Buy\Nsomething or leave.

135.0: \CYou are the boy Jess found, are you\Nnot? Welcome to our village. May\Nyou find safety and hope in the gods.
135.1: \CYes, I know, Alundra. Wendell has\Nsurvived. The gods held forth a thread\Nof salvation for his soul.\ALet us pray to the gods and thank\Nthem for their undeserved\Nbenevolence!\0000\Y
135.2: \CYou see. The gods do exist. They\Nexist in the hearts and minds of those\Nthat pray dearly to them\W2
135.3: \CHave you no respect for the powers\Nof salvation? On your knees!\ALet us pray to the gods and thank\Nthem for the undeserved kindness\Nthey have extended!\0000\Y
135.4: \CAre you upset that we have no\Nstatues, no symbols of our gods?\AIn this land, it is a crime to worship\Nby means of such artefacts and\Ntrinkets\W2\AThe law seems at once rash and\Nfoolish to me, but I have no control\Nover such matters.
135.5: \CI have received a vision. Our world\Nhas witnessed the second coming of\Nevil!\AWe must join together to resist it or\Nall will certainly be lost in a fiery\Napocalypse!
135.6: \CThe coal mine was in the Murgg\NWoods? \W2\T\W2\THow intriguing.
135.7: \CHear me, O guardians of our fragile\Nsouls!\AI beg only that you remember the\Ngood deeds of Olen, Jaylen, Zane,\Nand Lyman as they stand before you.
135.11: \BThe book is wedged so tightly into\Nthe opening that it refuses to budge.
135.13: \CIt seems to be a perfect fit, Alundra.\ALet's turn it and see what happens\W2
135.15: \CIt\W2moved! By the gods, Alundra!\NBehold! A concealed staircase!\AI'll bet you 100 gilder Ronan not\Nonly knows about it\W2he uses it.\NBut\W2for what?
135.16: \CWhere are you going, Alundra? This\Nis no time to give up! Come back\Ninside\W2
135.18: \C\W2\T\W2\TLord Melzas! Give ear to the\Nsupplication of your humble servant.\N\AI beg of you, oh great one, to give me\Npower to destroy the demon that\Nis invading our dreams!
135.19: \CThis is Ronan's work. I'd bet your\Nlife on it. \W2\T\W2\T\W2\AJust kidding. A little humour to\Nlighten the heaviness of the moment,\Nmy studious friend\W2
135.20: \CNadia was one of your most faithful\Nbelievers, my lord\W2\AWhy did you let her perish when she\Nneeded your power the most? Help\Nyour humble servant understand\W2
135.21: \CHow dare you desecrate this holy\Nground with your blasphemous\Npresence! Leave here at once!
135.22: \CHave you heard of the one called\NMeia? The one with powers equal\Nto your own?
135.23: \CI shall never let you destroy this\Nvillage, heretic! I will fight your\Ncorrosive influence until death!
135.24: \CThe gods have shown me that it is\Nyou who have brought death and\Ndestruction to Inoa.
135.25: \CSoon, Alundra, you and the evil you\Npossess shall forever be cut off!
135.26: \CShe was so young\W2Sybill had\Nonly just begun her journey in life.
135.27: \CSybill would still be alive if not for\Nyou\W2you\W2Murderer! Stealer of\Ninnocent souls!
135.28: \BThe hideous thing that Ronan had\Nbecome has been slain!
135.30: \CThose who commit sins against the\Nguardians shall be punished. It is an\Nincontrovertible fact of our existence.
135.44: \CYou're fighting to save us, are you\Nnot, Alundra? \W2\T\W2\T\W2\AWe have lived with peace in our\Nhearts by praying to our gods.\N\ABut the gods have forsaken us and\Nchosen the Murgg as our eternal\Ntormentors, it seems.\AAnd, whether chosen or not, you\Nhave become our protector.\N
135.45: \CWe are experiencing the vile fruit\Nof the god's anger. The eruption is\Nbut a small sign of their displeasure.\AThere will be more\W2many more,\NI am certain\W2\N
135.46: \C\W2\T\W2\TWhat?! Bergus was\Ncaptured by the Murgg?\AAlundra, you must risk everything\Nto rescue that poor child from a\Ncertain, horrid fate\W2
135.50: \CThere is a draught coming from\Nsomewhere nearby\W2
135.51: \CHere. The air is coming from here.
135.52: \CAlundra?!\T\T\T ALUNDRA! If\Nyou're in there, come to the front and\Nopen the door, please.
135.53: \CThe gods are not merely part of our\Nlives, Alundra. The gods are our\Nlives.\AWait at Beaumont's house. It is there\Nthat your fate shall be determined\W2\N
135.60: \CDespite my efforts, you refuse to\Nleave this village, and you will not\Nbe forced out.\A\W2\T\W2your blood then rests on your\Nown head now, my foolish friend.\N
135.61: \CWell, well, Alundra. I see you are\Nwith Meia today.
135.62: \DThe statue of Melzas is hidden in the\Nbasement of this sanctuary. I can\Nfeel it even standing here!
135.63: \COh?\T\W2\T\W2\TThe gods have shown\Nthemselves to you, have they?\N
135.64: \D\W2\TYes, Ronan. It was wonderful.\NThey asked me to pray to their\Nvisage\W2
135.65: \C\W2\T\W2\TDo you think me so\Ndull as to believe you?\NIf you have seen anything at all,\Nit is a devil, not a god.\N\AYou want me to take you to the\Nstatue I keep, not to worship it, but\Nto destroy it.\AIf you underestimate me, you are\Nlikely to be severely disappointed,\Nchildren.
135.66: \DUnderstood, Ronan.\ANow get out of my way. And please\Ndon't try to prevent the inevitable\W2\N
135.67: \CHrmph! Arrogant girl. Beaumont\Nhas always known of the statue in\Nmy sanctuary.\AEveryone knows. And, they not\Nonly approve of it, dear child, they\Npray to it as well.\AHow would they react, I wonder, if\Nyou were to destroy the object of\Ntheir fevered supplication?\AI'd wager their reaction to be much\Nless favourable than you would hope,\Nlittle ones\W2

137.108: \CWhat is Ronan trying to hide? And\N\W2why? We must search until we\Nget to the bottom of this\W2
137.109: \CThis stand seemed a bit out of place,\Nand when I examined it more\Nclosely\W2it moved.\ANot much, but it DID move.\N\N
137.111: \CSomething is blocking it from\Nmoving any further.
137.112: \CWhat's that?\AYou say the book keeps vanishing\Nbefore you can lay your hands on\Nit?
137.113: \CCertainly, I'll help you. Besides, I'm\Na scholar. Locating lost and rare\Nbooks is my speciality!\AA little scholar humour there\W2uh,\Nwell, never mind.\N
137.114: \CAlundra! Come quickly! I've found\Nyet another switch\W2
137.115: \CIt could be a trap. It could be\W2\Nanything. But we must try it\Nanyway, right?\301\Y
137.116: \CAll right. Here I go. Pushing the\Nswitch. Yes, indeed. I'm pushing\Nthis switch that could kill us\W2\A\W2\T\W2\TAre you sure we should try\Nthis switch?\N\301\Y
137.117: \CWhat the\W2?! That sounded like it\Ncame from the east wing!
137.118: \CAh\W2perhaps I should stay here while\Nyou investigate further\W2
137.119: \C\W2\T\W2\TI see.\AThe book seems to have a mind of its\Nown. But, I do have a plan! You chase\Nthe book while I wait here for it.\A\W2\T\W2What's that?\N\N\AWell, I came up with the plan, so you\Nget to chase the blasted thing around\Nthe room!
137.120: \CThis is probably the best place to\Ncatch the book, Alundra. So then,\Nwhat are you waiting for? Get to it!
137.121: \BThere is a small gap between two\Nof the volumes.
137.122: \BShall we put the book into the slot\Non the shelf?\301\Y
137.123: \BAlundra slides the Book of Runes\Ninto the space on the shelf.\AIt is so tightly wedged into the space\Nthat it cannot be removed again.\N
137.124: \BSadly, Alundra does not have a\Nbook.\ACoincidentally, he is also lacking a\Nlibrary card, making him a prime\Ncandidate for the RIF program.
137.125: \CIf only we could find an easy way\Nto move this monstrous pedestal\Naside\W2
137.126: \CLook here\W2that seems to be a\Nkeyhole of some sort in the side,\Nbut it's quite unusual\W2\AIn fact, I've never beheld its equal.\NI doubt I could fashion a key to fit\Nit.\AI believe Ronan must have hidden\Nthe key to this somewhere in the\Nsanctuary. We must find it!
137.127: \CHa! Now\T\W2\T\W2\Tyou are one with us, my\Nfriend! You shall become just as\Nwe\W2no better, no worse!

138.0: \CThis is\T\W2\T\W2a statue of worship\NA statue for the gods!\AThe King made it a crime to\Nworship these idols.\N\AAnd here you are, breaking the\Nlaw! Why Ronan? Why?\N
138.1: \CNow that the gods are not seen,\Nthey have been all but forgotten by\Nsinful mankind\W2\ACalled upon by us only in times of\Ndire need, the gods are angry for\Ntreating them this way.\AI am a faithful servant of the gods,\Nand I continue to respect and honour\Nthem.\AI have violated the King's law since\Nits inception. Yet, I have not hidden\Nthat fact.\AMost of the good people here know\Nof my \W3crime.\W4\N
138.2: \CAre you saying the gods are angry\Nwith us, Ronan? That\W2they are\Nthe root cause of our nightmares?
138.3: \CThe only one who said the\Nnightmares were the work of evil\Nwas Meia.\AOr\T\W2\T\W2was it you, Alundra?\N\N
138.4: \CI don't\W2understand. Why are the\Ngods\W2who created us, now\Ntorturing and murdering us?
138.5: \CBecause we have betrayed them,\NSeptimus.\AWhen the King's foolish edict was\Nissued, we lost our ability to\Ncreate.\ASo, instead, we learned how to\Ncontrol and manipulate our own\Ndreams.\AWe sought out happiness in the\Nworlds within our own minds. The\Ndomain of our personal id.\ADon't you understand? It's not the\Ngods who are at fault! \W2it's us.\N
138.6: \CLet's go, Alundra. Talking to this\Nzealot is a waste of time.
138.7: \CRonan\T\W2\T\W2We shall carry on in\Nour fight against this evil that has\Ncome upon us.\AEven if we find ourselves battling\Nmerciless gods themselves! For a\Ngod without mercy is a demon!
138.8: \CHa, ha, ha! Oh, really? I'm sure the\Ngods are cowering in fear at your\Nill-thought blasphemy, Septimus!
138.10: \DUntil all this has ended, we will\Nstay here, inside the sanctuary.\AThese strong walls will keep us\Nsafe if and when the Murgg attack\Nagain.
138.11: \CThey do not need to break down\Nthe walls! They can attack us\Nfrom our own dreams!\AOr have you already forgotten?!\N\N
138.12: \DBoth Bergus and Nestus are here\Nwith us, Gustav!
138.13: \DCalm down, Gustav! I can\Npromise you the Murgg cannot\Ninvade our dreams.\ABergus and Nestus were a special\Ncase.\N
138.14: \CFine\T\W2\T\W2I have no\Nreason to distrust you, Meia.\ABut tell me this\W2If Melzas\Ninvades our nightmares, what\Nthen?\ANot even you and Alundra\Ncombined could save us all.\N\AAll we are doing is waiting for\NMelzas to extinguish our lives!\N
138.15: \DSilence! We are not here to die,\NGustav! We came here to join\Nforces and fight for life!!\AEveryone here has suffered the\Nloss of a loved one\W2so spare\Nus your self-pity!
138.16: \CPlease, everyone! Let's calm\Ndown and listen carefully.\AOur power to create was taken\Nfrom us by Melzas.\N\ASo, we developed the power to\Ncontrol our dreams\T\W2\T\W2\Nand that is our secret weapon.\AWe can use that power to control\Nthe power that Melzas exerts over\NAlundra.
138.18: \CWe are going to join hands and\Nrelax until we drift into sleep.\AAnd then, we shall dream the\Nexact same dream.\N
138.19: \DYou mean\W2\T\W2\Twe are\Ngoing to combine our dreams?\ATurn our \W3weak\W4 dreams\Ninto a single \W3strong\W4 one?\N\AWe will arrive in the same\Nnightmare as\W2\Tdream\W2\T\Nwarriors?
138.20: \COversimplified, but yes.\AWe shall dream about an\Nincredibly strong hero.\AA hero under our control, who\Nshall join with Alundra to destroy\NMelzas.
138.21: \CTo tell the truth, Beaumont, I can't\Npicture what a \W3hero\W4\Nwould look like.\AI think we should dream of\Nsomeone we all know well\W2\None we can easily conjure up\W2
138.22: \DI agree with Yuri. If even one of\Nus has a different mental image\Nthan the others\W2
138.23: \CI have an idea\W2Why don't we\Nsimply visualise Alundra?\AI think we are all very familiar\Nwith his appearance\W2\N\AAnd I cannot imagine anyone\Nmore heroic. Does anyone\Ndisagree?
138.28: \DWait! Not yet!\001\W2\T\W2\TBefore we begin to\Ndream, there is something we\Nmust do.\AAlundra is about to risk his life\Nfacing Melzas. Think about it.\N\ADon't you think there is\Nsomething we can do for him?\N
138.29: \DWhat do you mean?\002\Y\N\W2\T\003Oh, now I know!
138.32: \CWell, then. Enough talk. It is\Ntime for us to dream.
138.33: \DThis is what we feel. Alundra,\Nwe know you can defeat Melzas.\AWe give you all of our faith\W2\Nour heart \W2 our strength.\N
138.34: \CNava should know almost\Nanything you want to know about\NMelzas.
138.35: \DThis is your home now, Alundra.\NWe are your friends\W2your\Nfamily.\AYou must come back. Promise\Nme\W2\N
138.36: \EYou aren't a peasant\W2You're a\Nhero.\AIf you defeat Melzas, I promise to\Nbe your slave. But only for a day!\N
138.37: \DThis old woman can see quite\Nwell despite her years.\A\W2\T\W2\TThe darkness trembles\Nat your approach.\N\AGo now, and engage in the battle\Nof dreams.\N
138.38: \CAlundra\W2I am starting to\Nbelieve that you are truly our\Nsaviour. Take care, good friend.
138.39: \DThe souls of our loved ones must\Nbe avenged. Remember them as\Nyou fight against Melzas\W2
138.40: \EHi, Alundra.\NI am going to dream now. Please\Ndon't die like Dad and Grandpa.\AI don't want to cry anymore\W2
138.41: \EI'm scared, Alundra. Melzas is a\Ngod! How can you fight him\Nwithout being killed?
138.42: \DI will fight with you in my dream,\NAlundra. Destroy Melzas\W2for\Nall of us!
138.43: \CElene was racked with\Nexcruciating pain when she\Nexpired, Alundra.\APromise me you will make\NMelzas feel the same pain.\N\AI want you to make him suffer\Nbefore you end his pathetic\Nexistence.
138.45: \DMelzas' sanctuary is in the lake\Nto the north, within the sunken\Npalace.
138.46: \CI have trusted you in the past,\NAlundra. Don't let us down!
138.47: \DFare thee well, Alundra.\NReturn to us safely.
138.48: \DI want nothing more than to fight\Nwith you, Alundra.\AThe fact that I cannot angers me,\Nyet, at the same time, fills my\Nheart with sadness\W2

290.0: \DAlundra! Wake up! We have a big\Nproblem!\AAlundra! Are you awake?\N\N\0000\Y
290.1: \DBergus has been kidnapped by the\NMurgg. We have to find him\Nbefore\W2
290.2: \DThis is not the time for games,\Nsleepyhead! This is serious!
290.4: \BWith the permission of the dragon\NWilda, Alundra obtained the sixth\Ncrest.\AOnly one more and Alundra would\Npossess them all.\N\ABut he was too preoccupied with\Nother matters to realise it.\N\AHe worried about Ronan. When\Nwould he break his silence? And\Nhow?\AAnd what of the Murgg? When\Nwould Melzas command them to\Nattack?\AThe night was quiet. A deafening\Nsilence closed in on Alundra\W2\N

291.0: \CDid you hear about Bergus? That\Npoor boy must be scared out of his\Nwits.\AI'm consulting my books to figure\Nout how we can rescue the lad\W2\N\AWhy don't you go to his house and\Nask his parents what they saw?\N

292.0: \CThank you for coming at such a late\Nhour, Alundra. Has anyone told\Nyou what happened? No?\AI sent Bergus and Nestus to sleep\Na few hours ago. The three of us\Nwere down here talking\W2\AWhen we heard the sound of\Nshattering glass\W2\N\AI ran upstairs and saw the Murgg\Nleaping out the window with\NBergus.\AHe looked at me and tried to\Nscream\W2I ran after them, but\Nthe darkness embraced them\W2\AAnd, my poor son was in their dirty\Ngrip\W2\N\AThis is my worst nightmare realised,\NAlundra.\N\APlease! There's no one else in this\Nvillage I can turn to for help\W2\N
292.2: \CWhat can I do to help? I shall do\Nanything you ask of me, Septimus.\NAnything to save my son.
292.3: \CI am not quite sure, but if Bergus can\Nbe saved, will you do it?
292.4: \CAlundra\T\W2\T\W2\TI love my son so\Nmuch. Please do what you can.
292.5: \CWe should have been more\Ncareful\W2and now, Bergus will\Npay for our folly with his very\W2\AOh, my grandson, what have we\Ndone?\N
292.8: \D\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2Nestus is\Nfinally asleep. He's been crying\Nalmost as much as I.
292.9: \DI beg you to bring back my son\Nsafely, Alundra.
292.11: \DHow much longer is he going to\Nkeep us\W2
292.13: \DI hope you have a good reason\W2
292.14: \D\W2\T\W2\TYou're right.\NBecause they are twins, Bergus\Nand Nestus are as of one mind.\AYou can enter the dream of\NNestus\W2and return to the\Nwaking world next to Bergus.\ABut both of them need to be asleep\Nbefore you can travel across their\Ndreams.
292.15: \DI will stay here. Be careful.\NI\W2\T\W2\Talways worry about\Nyou, Alundra.
292.16: \CI am sorry, but I must complete my\Nresearch.
292.17: \CYes, it is. I have learned of a way\Nfor us to find Bergus.
292.19: \CIt's incredibly simple. According to\Nmy three-volume dream reference\Nguide\W2\AIdentical twins not only look the\Nsame, but often have the same\Ndreams.
292.20: \CAlundra\T\W2\T\W2\Tthis is\Nsomething only you can do.\AI think we can assume that Bergus\Nhas been taken to the Giant Tree\NTower\W2\T\W2\T\AWhich means you would be\Nsurrounded by Murgg when you\Nawoke.\A\W2\T\W2\Tlisten. Don't underestimate\Nthe challenge you will face at that\Npoint, Alundra.
292.21: \CNestus has fallen into a deep sleep.\NQuickly! Enter his dream!
292.22: \CQuickly! Enter Nestus' dream while\Nyou have the chance!

293.0: \EAlundra!\NMy roof\W2my roof\W2my roof is on\N fire!
293.1: \CYou saved Bergus and defeated\Nthe Murgg.\AAll I can do is thank you\W2again\W2for\Nyour heroism. You are all that most of\Nus have faith in anymore.\AThe survivors of the attack have\Ngathered here. You should speak with\Nthem to raise their spirits a bit.
293.4: \EPlease, Alundra! Kill the Murgg before\Nthey do anything else!
293.5: \EHey, Alundra!\AI heard that Mum and the others are at\Nthe Mayor's house, so I came here\Nto find them.\AAlundra, I'm scared. Things are\Nlooking pretty bleak, and I don't\Nthink you can fix them!
293.7: \BMyra lies quietly in death as\Nthe smoke bellows from her\Nbeloved abode\W2
293.40: \CBonaire\T\W2\T\W2\TBonaire is\W2\AMy son was my life. Bonaire was\W2\Neverything to me\W2

295.1: \EMum! You're okay! When I saw our\Nhouse on fire, I was SO afraid.
295.3: \CElene was back to herself again,\NAlundra.\AFor the first time in so very long. And\Nnow\W2she is gone.\N\AI will not rest until I have spilled the\Nblood of every Murgg that still draws\Nbreath!\A\W2until I destroy their lives the way\Nthey've obliterated mine!\N
295.4: \EDaddy! Grandpa! I'm so scared!\AMake it stop! Please make it STOP!!
295.5: \DOh, Bergus!\AI knew you would be all right. I just\Nknew. You've always been a fighter.
295.6: \DThank you, Alundra.\AI can never repay you\W2but I promise\Nto help you whenever I can.
295.7: \DMeade and Wendell were\W2fighting\Nthe Murgg\W2\T\APlease don't tell the children what\Nreally happened. I can scarcely\Nbear to think about it myself\W2
295.8: \CBy the gods\T\W2\T\W2\AMeade and Wendell were good men.\NTo think that both of them were\Nslaughtered by the cursed monkeys\W2
295.9: \CWe have to decide on a course of\Naction in light of this terrible new\Ntragedy, Alundra.\AI realise you just returned from a\Nlong journey, but can we begin the\Nmeeting at once?\0251\Y
295.11: \CAll right\T\W2\T\W2We shall wait a\Nshort while longer.
295.12: \DAlundra, I haven't seen Sierra around\Nhere.\AYou don't think she's been devoured\Nby the Murgg, do you?\N
295.13: \DThe Murgg have yet to complete their\Ndesolation\W2I can feel it\W2
295.14: \CWhere is Ronan? Has anyone seen\Nhim? No? I pray he's all right\W2
295.15: \CSmart little bastards\W2\AThey appeared on the second floor of\NWendell's house.\AAnd, they managed to cross from\NBergus' dream into Nestus'!\N\AThey don't possess the power to do\NTHAT by themselves, Alundra\W2\N
295.16: \DIf the Murgg come back, this village\Nwill be razed to rubble. Oh, Alundra\W2
295.17: \DI'll fight the gods themselves if that's\Nwhat it takes to restore peace to this\Nplace!
295.18: \DIf there were any more of the Murgg,\Nthis house would have been destroyed.
295.19: \EPeasant, when the Murgg come to eat\Nme, I want you to take my place!
295.20: \DI am so sorry, Alundra\T\W2\T\W2\T\AI did everything I could, but I couldn't\Nprotect the people of this village\W2\AAt least you're all right\W2I couldn't\Nbear to think what I would have done\Nhad you been injured\W2

298.12: \DI'm sorry Alundra. If you don't\Nhave enough Gilder, I can't really\Nhelp you\W2

298.16: \DOh, I am sorry to hear that.
298.17: \DAlundra, the Silver Armour has been\Nin my family for as long as our\Nfamily can remember. But\W2\AI want you to have it. Just promise\Nme you won't scratch it up too\Nmuch, okay?\AI'm gonna have to pass this down\Nto my kids someday, you know?\N

299.0: \CGood morning, Alundra. Remember\Nto return here later for the meeting.\AI have made my decision\W2and I\Nbelieve yours was made long ago.\N

299.4: \EI don't believe in a god, peasant. I\Ndon't believe in anything\W2
299.5: \DDon't cry, Nestus. You have to be\Nstrong. You have to be a man like\Nthey were.

303.0: \CYour instincts are right. Nava is\Nnot a member of this village, nor\Nany other\W2and neither am I.\AWe are the Zolist. Our lifespans\Nhave been magically extended\Nbeyond that of humans\W2\AHe and I have lived here for more\Nthan 200 years.
303.1: \CBut, our duty is ended today. If we\Ndelay but one day more, Melzas will\Nshower our world with evil.\AWe have no choice but to raise\Nthe sanctuary from the lake and\Ndestroy Melzas first.\AGo to Nava, Alundra. He will\Nexplain the rest.
303.2: \CNava has passed from this\Nworld?\AThough I am filled with sorrow,\NI am grateful that you were with him\Nas he passed from this world.\A
303.3: \CI'm off to the mine, lad. The sooner I\Nget my work done, the sooner I can\Ncome back to Kisha!
303.4: \CWith a Mining Bomb, this work\Nwould be finished in 8.3 seconds\Nflat.\AWell, all right, give or take a tenth.\N\N\AWhat I wouldn't give for one of\Nthose babies right now. You know,\NJess used to make them\W2
303.5: \BWh\W2\W2day\W2\W2,\Nthe night\W2\W2was\W2\W2.\NThose born\W2\W2\Adarkness\W2\W2per\W2\W2\Nglow\W2\W2eternal\W2\W2.\NIt's too dusty to read.\NShould Alundra clean it?\0\Y

304.1: \CI don't like the one to my left. If I\Nam revered after him, I'll be mad!\0001\Y
304.2: \CLet's go. Don't be afraid. Tell me\Nthe thoughts of your heart.\0002\Y
304.3: \CI am going to follow the one up\Nthere. So don't come to me before\Nthe one I follow.\0003\Y
304.4: \CWrong, wrong, wrong!\NThe top one should be after me!\AAnd after that, the one on my left\Nside! That's the only way!\N\0004\Y

304.8: \CIt's too late. Go home, simple one!\NYou should have come before the\None to the right.\0008\Y
304.9: \CI am afraid of the one on top for\Npersonal reasons.\APerhaps you should meet with\Nhim first.\0009\Y

The demon\Nresides near this cursed village.\AHe has paralysed these poor folk with\Nfear\W2They are as cattle being led\Nto the inevitable slaughter.\AIf they only knew what I do,\NMother.\W2\NIt is my duty to destroy him. I will not\Nfail, Mother. I cannot fail\W2\N

311.0: \CHoo dawg! This is a pleasant surprise!\NIt looks as if I finally have a paying\Ncustomer!
311.1: \CYou goin' buy somethin', or you just\Ngonna stand there lookin' stupid?
311.2: \CI reckon that tree blocking the bridge\Nmusta up'n disappeared, I do. I'm\Nthinkin' business is gonna pick up!
311.3: \CEverythin' in Lurvy's shop is one of\Na kind, uh-huh. An' don't go thinkin'\N'bout gettin' no better prices elsewhere!
311.4: \CWhat in blazes are ya doin'? Are ya\Ntryin' ta bed me, ya shameless\Npervert?!\AGet outta my bedroom! Don't make\Nme come up there!\N
311.6: \CYou ain't told my little secret to\Nnobody, and I 'preciate that. Thank\Nye.\AI reckon I got to keep your secrets,\Ntoo, uh-huh, I do.\N
311.7: \CThat there Medicinal Herb'll run you\N4 Gilder. Okay?\0100\Y
311.8: \CA Strength Tonic'll run ya 12 Gilder\Nthese days. Soun' like a deal?\0100\Y
311.9: \CA Magic Elixir costs 24 Gilder.\NYa still in the market for one?\0100\Y
311.10: \CI reckon I should charge 600 Gilder\Nfer that Wonder Essence, but I'll give\Nit ta ya fer only 500. Want it?\0100\Y
311.11: \CWhatsa matter? Ya dull or somethin?\NI reckon you ain't got space in your\Nbag fer nothin' else like that, mister.
311.12: \CYou ain't got enough Gilder, and this\Nstuff ain't for free. No way, no how.
311.13: \CWhere you goin'?! You ain't tryin' ta\Nrob me, are ya?
311.14: \CWhat you doin', boy?! Get outta my\Npersonal, private 'zecutive quarters!
311.17: \CGood eyes, boy. That there's a Leather\NVest of Armour.  Hasn't been popular\Nsince the Village Boys went out\W2\AIt's a steal of a deal, at only 120\NGilder, 'specially since that retro\Ncraze is 'bout ta kick in. Deal?\0100\Y
311.18: \CI don't need that thing no more 'cause\N\W2I'm too old to care! 400 Gilder'n\Nthe durn thing's yurs. Want it?\0100\Y
311.20: \CYou're a purty smart shopper, boy.\NGot you some good deals. Uh-huh.
311.21: \CI seen a lotta things, boy, but that's a\Nnew one on me. Uh-huh. Was the door\Ntoo hard to open? Um hmm?
311.22: \CI guess you figured out what I do\Nhere. Uh-huh. Go 'round town and\Ncollect garbage...\AI fix it, then I sell it. I ain't proud of\Nthat fact.\N\AAnd, I'd 'preciate it if ya didn't tell\Nnobody, seein' as I jus' got right in\Nthe head.
311.23: \CTell yew what. Ya need somethin'\Nfixed, bring it on in. I'll make it right\Nfor free\W2
311.24: \CI reckon I'd 'preciate it if you'd be so\Nkind as to use my front door from\Nnow on!
311.25: \CStrange things you're sellin'.\0101\NLemme see here\T\W2\T\W2It's old,\Nbut I can fix it. Should I get started?\0100\Y
311.26: \C\W2\T\W2\TYa wanna keep it a hunk of junk?\NI reckon you can do whatever catches\Nyour fancy with it!
311.27: \CCan't just give to it ya. Nuh-uh. How's\N'bout a measly 2163 Gilder?\0100\Y
311.29: \CBeen a long time since I banged\Narmour. Did a damned fine job, too.\NUh-huh, I did.\A\0101Purty, ain't it\T\W2\T\W2makes\Nme proud.
311.30: \BLurvy takes the dilapidated old\Narmour quite eagerly.
311.32: \CGet back in the store, ya wise-crackin'\Ncity-dweller!\N
311.33: \CFree of charge, just like I told ya.
311.37: \CWhat you doin'?! Don't be makin' a\Nmess, boy! I'll slap ya back inta\Ndiapers 'fore ya know what hit ya!
311.38: \CI reckon you better stop foolin'\N'round 'fore I give you a whuppin'!

312.54: \BWith the blessing of the Four\NGoddesses, show my kingdom\Nyour courage.
312.55: \BYou are the one who has been\Nblessed\W2Let me show you the\Nway!
312.56: \BWithout a key to unlock it, there's\Nno chance of it moving.
312.58: \C\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\AHe that treads foolishly into the sacred\Nkeep shall reap the pain of a thousand\Ncrushed souls!
312.59: \CHear my words, Releaser. I have\Ncome to be known as Jeal. I am also\None of the seven guardians\W2\AI was a metalsmith who sought to\Nunderstand the mysteries of life.\N\ATo stop the evil present in the mortal\Nrealm, I sacrificed my human form\Nand vanished into time. \AI have given thought to trusting the\Nlight of your soul to save this weary\Nland.\AHowever,\W2\T\W2\Tyou must bear\Nin mind that to defeat Melzas is to\Nrisk the end of reality itself!\A\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2If you can bear\Nthat risk, proceed.\N

312.70: \BLet the light of guidance show the\Nsign of contact\W2
312.71: \BPlease give me the life which is\Nborn of fire\W2
312.72: \BBless the destroyer of evil who\Nhides within the flowing waters\W2
312.73: \BYou petition the guardians to\Nopen the doors.\ARight Door:\AAsk the one up and on the other side.\N\ACentre Door:\AAsk the one to the left and at the\Ntop class and the one on the right\Nsecond from the bottom .\ALeft Door:\AAsk the one closest.
312.81: \BThe wall is flawed by a deep fissure.
312.83: \CI see\T\W2\T\W2it has all become\Ncrystal clear\W2You are the\NReleaser, Alundra.
312.84: \COne who's inner strength and resolve\Nis as potent as yours is a rare find,\Nindeed.\AIf you have resolved to fight to the\Ndeath, you may be able to challenge\NMelzas himself.
312.90: \EThis pump is the heart of our great\Nwaterway. We will never allow one\Nto destroy it! Die, trespasser!
312.91: \BThere is a distant sound of gurgling\Nwater.
312.92: \BThe water is too deep. Further access\Nis impossible\W2
312.95: \DI am at once amazed and proud that\Nyou have progressed this far,\NReleaser.\AI am Stenia, Queen of the waters.\NYour actions have been shown to\Nmy heart by the rivers and oceans.\AOver the course of human history,\Nthere have been many gods.\N\ANot long ago, there was a race of\Ngiant gods called the Gazeck.\N\AYou have met one of them\W2Nirude.\NThe Gazeck were carved from stone\Nby the hands of ancient humans.\AThe seven Gazeck were revered and\Nfeared by the ancients\W2\N\ASoon, their prayers gave life to the\NGazecks. They literally became\Nwhat humans believed them to be.\ABut the Gazeck did not want to share\Nthe power of human prayer.\N\AThey fought each other for it\W2they\Nkilled each other for the prize of\Nhuman adulation.\AAll but one of them perished. \TOnly\NNirude declined to fight his fellow\Ngods.\AHe watched with a heavy heart as his\Nbrothers slaughtered one another.\N\ABut when the killing subsided, Nirude\Nfound that he was a god no more.\N\AThe ancient humans had long since\Nlost faith in the warring Gazeck.\N\AAnd, a god cannot exist without the\Nfaith of others\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\N\ASoon, another god was born from the\Nprayers of the people.\T That one was\T\N\W2Melzas.\ABut he was not the god of eternal\Npeace for which the humans had\Nprayed.\AHe was even more flawed than the\NGazecks had become, using fear to\Ngain the faith of humans.\ABut Melzas feared the wisdom of\Nhumans. He knew that they could\Nstrip him of power.\ATherefore, he began slaying\Nwhomever seemed to threaten his\Nexistence.\ASomehow, you have managed to\Nescape his machinations to this\Npoint\W2\A\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2
312.96: \DMelzas has been watching us,\NAlundra. He has used my own water\Nagainst me\W2Take this, Alundra!
312.97: \DMelzas will soon destroy this\Nplace.\A\999\Y\ALeave here, Alundra! You must\Nhurry! The destruction comes!\N
312.98: \BA low rumble of falling rocks can\Nbe heard.
312.100: \BHe that does not fear the flame\Nshall gain mastery over it for\Nall eternity.
312.101: \CWhat have we here?\AYet another greedy human seeking\Nto claim the power of flame for\Nhimself?\AAll right, foolish one. Let's play a\Ngame of skill with my ball of\Neternal damnation!\APrepare to come to terms with your\Nlimitations, human!\N
312.103: \CYou're different from those that\Nhave come before\W2but you have\Nnot proven yourself worthy, yet.\AFollow the course of wisdom\Nemblazoned within your very soul\Nto meet your destiny.
312.104: \CIn the shadow of flame your\Npath must lie, until the time the\Nmotion dies\W2
312.105: \CIf you fail to finish upon the sign\Nof the flame, the power shall not\Nremain yours to command.
312.107: \CYou have indeed proven yourself\Na master of the flame! Take this\Nas proof of your mastery!
312.108: \CMay the power of flame never\Nleave your command!

346.4: \F\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\NYou are the one whom Lars termed\Nthe Releaser?
346.5: \FThe Guardians have become senile\Nin their old age\W2\AWhy else would they entrust the\Ncrests to a bumbling child such\Nas yourself?\AAh, well. That debate carries no real\Nmerit now. I have no time to ponder\Ntheir actions.\AYou have achieved the wonder of\Ngaining my full attention, trivial\None.\AAnd, now that you have come this far,\Nyou shall find that your fate is merely\Nto weep bitterly in the face of defeat!
346.7: \FMy bloodthirsty minions shall\Nsatisfy your death wish\W2behold!
346.8: \FWhy do you defer the fate that awaits\Nyou, boy? Submit to destiny and free\Nyour soul!\AFor no matter how many tears you\Ncry\W2 or how desperately you beg\Nfor mercy\W2\T\W2\TYou shall perish!
346.9: \FY\W2You! How dare you seek to\Nhumiliate me in my own sanctuary!\AFor your defiance, you shall drink\Nof the bitter cup of desolation I have\Nprepared, insolent one!
346.10: \FHow\T\W2\T\W2\THow can this be? How\Ncan an insolent child stand before a\Ngod?\ACurse you, Releaser! Curse you!!\NWithout you, the mortals would have\Nperished!\AInstead, I have come to this\Nhumiliating end at the hand of a mere\Nboy\W2
346.11: \FArrhhh! Your victory shall never\Nbe complete, Releaser!\AThe peace you and the other mortals\Nlong for shall never be fully\Nrealized.\AAs long as mortals harbour darkness\Nwithin their hearts, evil shall exist.\NIt is an incontrovertible fact\W2\AAnd darkness resides within every\Nmortal heart. Even yours, Alundra!\NGrahhhhhhhh!
346.12: \CAlundra! Your victory has nearly\Nbeen realised. Listen carefully to the\Nwords I speak!\AYou must burn Melzas' remains with\Nthe sacred fire to destroy him for all\Neternity!
346.13: \CYou have exceeded my expectations,\NReleaser. Well done!\ABut now is not the time to revel in the\Nsweet intoxication of victory.\N\ANow that Melzas has perished, the\Nsanctuary cannot remain standing\Nfor long.\AYou must escape before the walls\Ncollapse and the castle crumbles into\Nthe lake!
346.14: \CWhat's the matter, Alundra? Has the\Nstrain of battle addled your young\Nbrain?\AListen to the urgent message I bear!\NYou must burn Melzas' remains with\Nthe sacred fire!\AIt is the only way to destroy him for\Nall time\W2\N
346.22: \D\W2\TBergus, no! You must sleep\W2\Nyou have to dream!\AIf you don't, Alundra's life will be in\Ngrave danger\W2\N
346.23: \EBut, Mum, I woke up because I heard\Nthe sound of Alundra's voice!\A\W2\T\W2\TYou must've heard it, too!\N\N
346.24: \DDear son, Alundra is not here. There\Nis no way you could have heard his\Nvoice!\AGo to sleep\W2quickly now!\W2\N\N
346.26: \DNestus\T\W2\T\W2\TWe don't have the time\Nfor this!\AAlundra went to do battle with\NMelzas to save the lives of the people\Nof this land\W2
346.29: \DIt's not\W2my imagination.\AI really can hear him! Alundra!\NIt's Alundra!
346.30: \CWith all due respect, Rumi, I think\Nyou and your children are still a little\Ngroggy\W2
346.34: \CWhat's going on? You aren't\Ndreaming, and yet you can see and\Nhear Alundra!
346.35: \DUh\T\W2\T\W2? Yes, I can see a light.\NSmall, but strong!
346.36: \D\W2\T\W2\TI think we succeeded!\AThis must mean that our dreams and\Nprayers reached Alundra's heart!
346.37: \DOh, Alundra\W2Please be careful!\NYou must return to us!
346.38: \DAlundra, you are a boy no longer.\NYou have grown into a strong, brave\Nman.\AEven Melzas will not stand before\Nyou for long\W2I can just feel it\W2\N
346.39: \CAlundra, I know you will fight\Nthrough the obstacles in your\Npath\W2be strong!
346.40: \CJess is looking down upon you and\Nsmiling, Alundra. He knows you\Nshall deliver us from evil.
346.41: \EHey, you! Don't doubt yourself!\NI\W2believe in you!
346.42: \DMy prayers and my heart are with\Nyou\W2please take strength from that!
346.43: \CI can hear your cries of victory\Nalready!
346.44: \DAlundra, can you hear our voices?\NAnd,\W2 our prayers?
346.45: \EIf we can hear his voice, he must be\Nable to hear ours!\W2\T\W2\TAlundra!\APromise me you'll come back to us!\N\W2\T\W2\TPromise!\N
346.46: \ENo way Melzas can beat Alundra!\NHe's too strong\W2and too cool!
346.48: \EYou must emerge victorious! I'm\Ncounting on your skill!
346.49: \CYou have risked your life to fight for\Nours.\AIf anyone deserves our adulation, it's\Nyou, Alundra\N\AFor you are truly a deliverer from our\Ndark, cold night\W2\N
346.50: \DOh, Alundra, my heart is filled with\Nregret\W2\AI should have gone with you, even\Nthough you did not want me to risk\Nmy life.\ANow I can only wait here to see if\Nyou live or die\W2\Toh, Alundra!\NFor my sake, you MUST live!
346.52: \BAlundra hears and feels the voices\Nof his friends and their prayers\W2
346.53: \BThe thoughts of the united villagers\Nheal Alundra's wounded body and\Nrefreshes his soul\W2
346.56: \DThe long night has at last come to an\Nend. You are the sun, Releaser!
346.57: \CI will picture items in my mind and\Ntry to send them to you\W2

I am sorry to wake\Nyou at such a late hour, but I must\Nask a favour of you\W2\AWill you show me the face of one\Nwrithing in the midst of unbearable\Npain?\AOr, rather,\W2Will you show me\Nthe sweet life that flows through\Nyour body like warm wine?\AHa ha ha\W2Show me, Alundra!!\N\N

360.0: \C\W2\T\W2\TNo! Kline is gone!\AI have the ominous feeling something\Nis about to happen\W2Let's go find\Nhim before it does!

361.1: \CEveryone\T\W2\T\W2\Tplease listen!\AWe have to decide on our next course\Nof action, and quickly.
361.2: \CI think even the most faithful of us\Nrealises the truth by now.\AThe reason for all the nightmares\T\W2\T\N\W2and the reason for the Murgg\Nattacks.
361.3: \CThe gods\T\W2we once knew do not\Nwatch over us any longer\W2
361.4: \CRonan, we have been praying to a\Ndemon in the guise of a god of light.\AAnd that demon, Melzas, seeks to\Ndestroy us. It has become an\Nundeniable fact\W2
361.5: \CWe should go to the Murgg Woods\Nand burn it into oblivion!
361.6: \CHrmph! You have grown cowardly\Nin your old age, Yustel! We must\Nact decisively!
361.7: \DThere are not enough of us to fight,\NGustav.\AAnd I have already seen enough of us\Nkilled by those cursed monkeys to\Nchance to see any more.
361.8: \CCalm down, Gustav.\AI understand your desire for revenge,\Nbut we must think this through.\AI believe that we must combine our\Nthoughts into a single, powerful\Nwhole.
361.9: \CWhen we burned our idols and\Nstopped our worship\W2Melzas took\Naway our ability to create.
361.10: \CSo you're saying we never lost the\Npower to create in the first place?\NThat it was all an illusion?
361.11: \CIf we combine the power of our\Ncollective subconscious, I believe\Nwe CAN defeat Melzas, then.
361.12: \CYou know I'm right.\AI can tell by the looks on your faces!
361.13: \C\W2\T\W2\TYes.\AI agree with Septimus. We must\Ncombine our minds to form a single\Npowerful thought!
361.14: \CTo think it was our own god who\Ncaused our nightmares\W2a destroyer\Nof our own fabrication. Terrifying!
361.18: \CBeaumont\W2\NHave Alundra and his friends turned\Nyou into a blasphemer?
361.19: \CAre you prepared to betray our gods as\Nthe others have? To cast aside your\Nvery faith itself?
361.20: \CYou're all fools! Why do you\Nalways expect more from the gods?\AWhy are you not satisfied with prayer\Nand simple faith in the powers above\Nand their infinite wisdom?\AWith the knowledge that the gods are\Nwatching over us and guiding us?\N\AWhy should the gods have to prove\Nthemselves to you time and again?\NOr to anyone, for that matter?
361.21: \CWhat are you talking about?\AInstead of that, the gods have given\Nyou the power to control your dreams!
361.25: \C\W2\T\W2\TI will curse you. I shall\Ncurse you for the rest of your\Nmiserable existence!!
361.26: \DThe gods do not exist to watch over\Nus anymore. All we have been left\Nwith is a malicious tormentor!
361.27: \DThat's right. Melzas has abused and\Nbetrayed us!
361.29: \CI\T\W2\T\W2\Tthink so, too.\AIf there really were gods, they would\Nnever do such terrible things to us.
361.30: \CThat is right.\AIf this is how the gods repay us for\Nour prayer and devotion\W2
361.31: \DYou are all wrong.\AYou fail to understand what is truly\Nhappening.
361.32: \DI did not understand it fully myself\Nuntil a few moments ago\W2\AYou think that Melzas became angry\Nwith us when we stopped praying to\Nhim.\AHe punished us by taking away our\Npower to create. But that is not what\Nreally happened.\AWhen we prayed to our statues and\Nidols, Melzas was strong.\N\AAnd, when the statues were burned,\Nthe people stopped worshipping.\N\AMelzas could feel his strength begin\Nto ebb\W2he had to realize what\Nwas causing it to happen.\APerhaps he wondered what would\Nhappen if we started praying again\W2\N\ABut, instead of Melzas, we prayed\Nto a new god? Melzas was\T\W2afraid.\N\AFrightened that we might create a god\Nin his place. Afraid that he would\Nperish and be forgotten.\ATo preserve himself, Melzas had to\Nmake certain that we kept praying to\Nhim alone.
361.33: \DMelzas never stole away our power\Nto create,\W2because he never\Ncould.\AInstead, he went into our hearts and\Nmade us believe we had lost them.\N\AMelzas is nothing more than a vulture\Npicking at the exposed remains of our\Nvulnerable spirits!\AWhen we thought our power to create\Nhad vanished, our bodies and minds\Nreacted.\AWe gained the ability to control our\Nown dreams. That made Melzas even\Nmore fearful of us!\AWe were becoming more powerful than\Neven Melzas.\N\AAnd that is when he decided he had\Nto kill the most powerful of us.\N
361.34: \DSuch bitter irony, isn't it? Fighting\Nagainst the very god we created as a\Nresult of our faith\W2\AThe greatest battle lies before us. It is\Nthe battle with our legacy\W2with\Nourselves!
361.35: \CThis, then, is a choice we all have to\Nmake. Continue to worship Melzas\Nas a god\W2\AOr, challenge him with the powers\Nwe've amassed at the risk of our\Neternal souls!\AI know that I need some time to decide.\NI think we all do. But time is a luxury\Nwhich we cannot afford\W2\ATomorrow at noon, we shall take a\Nvote and decide our everlasting\Ndestiny.
361.36: \DI'd like you to stay at our house\Ntonight. I'd feel so much safer if you\Nwere there.
361.39: \CI think we should all get some rest.\AYou are all welcome to stay here,\Neven if your homes are still standing.\ASafety in numbers, as the saying\Ngoes\W2\N

380.50: \DOh, Alundra, my heart is filled with\Nregret\W2\AI should have gone with you, even\Nthough you did not want me to risk\Nmy life.\ANow I can only wait here to see if\Nyou live or die\W2\Toh, Alundra!\NFor my sake, you MUST live!

388.1: \EHere we end your advance, now\Nand forever!
388.2: \EFormation 42! Ready the brain\Npicks! Take him down\W2NOW!
388.3: \E\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2! Invader has been sighted!\NActivate the trap\W2\TNOW!
388.4: \EI praise your lofty efforts in making it\Nthis far, infidel. However, I must\Nput an end to your folly here\W2
388.5: \EDo you sometimes hear the words\Nyet not understand? I said IT'S\NOVER!
388.6: \BThe switch must be activated to\Nallow passage.\APress each lever once, then twice\Nin alternating order to proceed.\N
388.7: \BThe engine room is directly below\Nthis area. The switches must be\Nactivated correctly to proceed.\APress the levers in this order to\Nactivate the switches: left, right,\Nleft, left, right, right.
388.8: \EYou will not succeed, infidel!\NBehold! Even how, your life\Nseconds are numbered!
388.9: \EDharmaka!\T\W2\T\W2\Tyou are much\Nmore resourceful than I had thought.\NTry this on for size!
388.10: \EDharmaka!\T\W2\T\W2\Tthat didn't seem\Nto work. How about we run away\Nlike girls!?
388.11: \FYou have desecrated the sanctity of\Nmy ancient home. You must be an\Nagent of Melzas\W2\AIt seems that you are not my enemy,\Nhowever. But, neither have you\Nproven yourself my ally\W2
388.12: \FSuch resourceful survival skills can\Nonly be\W2Wait\T\W2\Tthat crest!\NYou are the Releaser\W2
388.13: \FI am Nirude, Releaser. You must\Nknow that I am one of the seven\NGuardians.\AI stand alone as the sole survivor \Nof the giant tribe. \W2\T\W2\T\W2\N\AThe prayers of Miming and his\Npeople have sustained me these\Nmany years of solitude\W2\AHowever, even the power of prayer\Nhas its limitations.\N\APlease accept my apology for\Ndoubting you, Releaser.\N\AI sense the courage and sincerity\Nwithin your soul.\N\AHmmm, I see. Nava sent you, did\Nhe? That is excellent.\N\AIt proves he has chosen to fight\NMelzas at last!\N\AI have waited for that confrontation\Nfor many, many years. I know you\Nshall emerge victorious!
388.14: \F\W2\T\W2\THmmm? Let me handle\Nthis, Alundra. Step back.
388.15: \FZorgia\T\W2\T\W2\T\NYou betrayed Wilda\W2\NYou betrayed the Gazeck.\AAnd now, you have taken the foul\Nside of Melzas.\N\AYou are a mercenary bastard,\Ndeserving only death!\N
388.16: \F\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\NTsk, tsk, Nirude. You have quite\Nthe sharp tongue today!\AHssss\W2Why must you use words\Nso sharp as to cause pain and hurt?\N\ABecause you once cared for me, I\Nplanned to spare you.\N\ABut now\W2your little speech has\Nchanged all that.\N\ALord Melzas has ordered your\Ndeath, and I'm now inclined to give\Nhim what he demands!
388.17: \FSuch an ugly scene. And, it's only\Ngoing to get uglier,\W2if I have\Nany say in the matter\W2\A\W2which, unfortunately for you, I\Ndo. Your turn Alundra. It's time to\Nbleed\W2
388.18: \FNot that I hold a grudge, of course.\NI'm just following the orders of my\Nlord and master, Melzas.\AA very prudent course of action,\Ngiven his power, wouldn't you\Nsay?\AIf you must hate someone, hate\NMelzas, not me. I'm just a pawn,\Nbound in gleeful servitude.
388.19: \F\W2\T\W2\THssss! Who alerted the munchkin\Nbrigade?!! They come!!\N\AAren't you lucky, Alundra. It\Nappears that your little friends have\Narrived to save the day!
388.20: \FThe time has come for me to depart,\NDreamchild. But rest assured that\NI shall find you and finish this\W2\AUntil then, Dreamer, lead a happy\Nlife without regret.\W2you never\Nknow when it will all end\W2
388.22: \ELet me tear out his quivering gullet\Nwith my bare hands!
388.23: \ENo! Hold him down so we can beat\Nhim to death!
388.24: \EKill him! Slay him! Pick him!\NSmash him!\N
388.25: \FNo\W2my children.\AThis is not the one who did\W2this\Nto me. The one you would condemn\Nis the only one that can save you\W2
388.27: \FIt's true, King Miming.\AHis power will save this land and\Nreturn peace to the hearts and\Nminds of all\W2
388.30: \FAlundra, you possess a strong name\Nthat shall serve you well.\APlease take another thing that will\Nserve you in like manner.\N\AHere is my crest. Melzas sent his\Nminions to retrieve it, but they failed.\NUse it to destroy him!
388.31: \F\W2\T\W2\T My material form is at\Nan end, my children. Leave here,\Nlest you perish as well!
388.33: \FHave faith in yourself, Alundra.\NDespite the hardships, you shall\Nprevail!
388.35: \ELord Nirude would want us to help\Nyou, Alundra. Please accept this gift\Nto help your quest\W2
388.37: \EWe would join you in your struggle\Nagainst Melzas, but we must keep\Nour defences up here.\ABesides, from what I witnessed of\Nyour skills, you don't require help\Nfrom such weak ones as us\W2\AGood luck, Alundra!\N\N
388.38: \EThis is really embarrassing,\NAlundra. I'm so sorry I tried to slay\Nyou.\AUm, here take this as a kind of\Napology\W2\N
388.42: \EWe cannot let you live even one\Nmoment longer, assassin \W2\T\N\W2\Ttake this!
388.43: \EYou cannot run! Your only duty is\Nto DIE!
388.44: \EDharmaka! He's back!?\NPerhaps this will chill his blood!
388.45: \E\T\W2Whoops, wrong switch!\NEr,\W2This is not good. RUN!\NRun away!
388.47: \BA distant thump is heard, as if\Nsomething large were shifted\Noutside\W2\ALarge boulders also seem to have\Nfallen into the next room from\Nsomewhere above\W2
388.48: \ENot another inch! You won't get an\Ninch deeper into this cave!\T\W2\T\N\W2TRIP THE TRAP!
388.49: \E\W2I have been informed of the\Npresence of an intruder! Lock the\Nentrance at once!
388.52: \ELord Nirude is in grave danger\W2\NI will have to fight, irregularity or\Nno\W2
388.54: \EHeh heh\W2 You aren't too bright\Nto get caught in such a simple trap as\Nthis\W2\AOh well, live stupid, die stupid, I\Nalways say\W2\N
388.55: \BThe door is shut tight, and there\Ndoesn't seem to be any sort of\Nkeyhole.
388.56: \EWe have to protect Lord Nirude,\Neven at the expense of our lives!
388.59: \EHuh?\T\W2\T\W2\TAn invader?\NNo way!! I must report this to Lord\NMiming at once!
388.60: \EHe's travelled this far in the cave?\NActivate the trap at once!
388.61: \EAll right, that's IT!! No more\NMr. Nice Dwarf! This cannon\Nvolley should be the end of you!
388.62: \EDharmaka! You follow at the risk\Nof your life, infidel! You SHALL\Nperish!
388.63: \EYou're dead this time! Without a\Ndoubt in my superior midget mind!
388.64: \FI have created this fold in time-\Nspace with my magic.\AWe shall soon see whether you are\Nenemy or friend\W2warrior or\Ncoward!

389.0: \CWhat's the matter, kid? Ya look\Na might pale\W2\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2\AHmmm\W2you've been having the\Nsame troubling dream every single\Nnight?\AAye, It's the seasickness fogging\Nyour land lubbin' mind. It'll pass.\N\AIf you'll excuse me, I had better\Ntend to easin' the ship into port. It\Nshould be near...
389.1: \CWhat ya be wantin', boy? Have ya\Nforgotten where yer cabin is\Nagain?\999\Y
389.2: \CDamnation! For the FIFTH time, lad,\Nyer cabin is the one on the right!\AAye! You're certainly not the\Nsharpest cutlass on the rack\W2\N
389.3: \CGood. If ya were to ask me again, I'd\Nlock ya inside of it until we reached\Nport!
389.4: \CBeautiful, eh? I've been a sailor since\NI was a lad younger'n you\W2\A\W2An' I haven't yet tired of watching\Nthe waves roll across the pristine\Nwaters beneath the bow\W2
389.5: \DYou're headed for the village of\NInoa? That's a good distance from\NTorla, as I recall.\AWhat kind of business takes you to\Nsuch a remote place?\N
389.6: \CI'm returning to my beloved. I've\Nnearly forgotten how it feels to hold\Nher in my arms\W2\AAnd what of you? Why do you travel\Nto Torla?\N\A\W2\T\W2\T What? Your dreams led you to\Nthis ship? You ain't one of them freak-\Nboys, are ya?
389.7: \DI can't tell you how weary I am of\Nlooking at the sea and clouds for\Ndays.\AI'll be so happy to be on dry land\Nagain\W2\N
389.8: \CYou're making me nervous, kiddo.\AGo lie down for a while. Why not have\Nyourself another one of those freaky\Ndreams while you're at it!
389.9: \CYa best be taking the Captain's advice,\Nboy. I'll wake ya when the harbour is\Nin sight.
389.10: \CI think ya best be headin' back to yer\Nquarters, boy.\AThe horizon's looking dark as night,\Nand the sea's turning a might restless.\NThere's a storm brewin'\W2
389.11: \DThe ocean breeze is suddenly so cold\N\T\W2\T\W2I'm wondering if I should\Nhead inside before I catch a chill!
389.12: \D\W2\T\W2\TI had a dream. I remember\N\W2yes\W2we've been tricked!
389.13: \CYou must ask Jess\W2No, you must\Ndemand of Jess that he create a new\Nsword.\999\Y\AI don't want to die, Alundra. I want to\Nlive. Forever if it were possible.\998\Y\N\ABut defeating the demon is far more\Nimportant than any one life, including\997\Y\Nmy own.\996\Y
389.14: \C\W2This is the Holy Sword. I began work\Non it shortly after Lutas died\T\W2\T\W2\AWith this weapon, Alundra, you can\Nrestore peace to our world once and\Nfor all.\AYou can't let the sacrifice Lutas made\Nbe for naught!
389.15: \CListen to me. \TDon't think about this\Nvillage, or the people who live here.\AThink only of the demon you're about\Nto face. Think of how you plan to\Ndestroy him.
389.16: \FWell\T...\T...\TIt's finally here.\AI can't believe they didn't listen to me...
389.19: \CStand fast, everyone! I've sailed this\Nship through storms twice as\Nferocious!\999\Y
389.20: \CAye, listen to the Captain! The lady\Nof the sea could never raise a swell\Nstrong enough to polish off the Klark!\999\Y
389.22: \CCap...Captain!\1000\Y We're headed\Nstraight for the reef! Hold on! Sweet\Nmother of god, we're\W2 \999\Y
389.23: \CThere's a crack in the wall? \AWell, I'll be sure to fix it as soon as\Nmy friend and I finish this bottle of\Ngrog\W2\A\W2or when monkeys fly out of\Nyour arse. Whichever comes first,\Nsissy boy.
389.24: \CYou were screamin' in your sleep\Nagain last night, boy. I coulda sworn\Nya were on fire!
389.25: \CThere's a crack in the wall? \AYeah, yeah, yeah. What's the rush to\Nfix it? I'm in no hurry\W2\N
389.26: \CLast night I heard ya screamin' as if\Nyer soul was ablaze, boy! I tell ya, kid,\Nyer givin' me the shakes!
389.27: \CYou're feeling seasick? Arrr! Drop\Nanchor over the side, boy! I just\Nswabbed the bloomin' decks!
389.103: \C\W2\W2I am the one known as Lars.\NI am a wizard, and one of the\Nguardians of the seal.\NThe time grows short before I am\Nbound once more\W2\N\999\Y
389.104: \CCan you hear me, Releaser?\1001\Y\NNorth of Inoa is a deep, dark lake.\NBelow its murky surface, a wretched\Ndemon has slumbered for 1000 years.\NNow, the foul beast stirs once more\W2\1002\Y\NWe stand on the threshold\W2\N\N\1004\Y\999\Y
389.105: \FYou make me laugh, feeble one!\NNo one has the power to stop me now!\NEspecially not a miserable human.\1001\Y\999\Y
389.106: \CTell me, then, Melzas.\1001\Y\NIf humans are so powerless, how is\Nit that prosperity is yours only by\Nmeans of their efforts?\1004\Y\999\Y
389.107: \F\W2Don't you understand, Wizard?\NHumans have long since ceased being\Nof use to me.\NTheir presence in my reality has\Nbecome nothing more than a thorn\Nin my side. Soon, I shall\W2\T\W2\T\W2\NWhy do you snicker, old man? Do you\Ndare to mock my judgement?\999\Y
389.108: \C\1001\YI laugh because\T\W2\T\W2you're afraid!\NYou talk of destruction, yet you fear\Nthe strength of humanity.\1001\Y\NWhy else would you come here\Nnow, to stop me from sending my\Nmessage of redemption?\1002\Y\NAdmit your cowardice, foul fiend!\1004\Y\999\Y
389.109: \FI am not so cruel as to steal away\Nthe last shred of hope from one\Ndrawing his final breath.\NBelieve what you will, Lars.\N\W2\T\W2\TBut do tell me about this\Nperson you call the Releaser.\NWhat is his name? Or\W2hers?\1001\Y\999\Y
389.110: \CMy time in this world has come to\Nan end, Releaser.\NBut, I have served my purpose. You\Nnow know of the great power locked\Nwithin you.\1001\Y\NHeed my words, Releaser\W2Travel\Nto Inoa. Use your strength to stop\Nthe demon. I now travel to the next\Nworld\W2\1002\Y\N\T\W2\T\W2\T\W2Releaser!!\1005\Y\999\Y
389.111: \FHa, ha, ha\W2Today, it is Lars.\NTomorrow it is you, Releaser.\1005\Y\NAnd then, the end of mankind.\1005\Y\NIt is destiny...\1005\YIt is fate.\1005\Y\999\Y
